Q: Python smtplib returns 250 OK but Gmail recipient never receives email (company domain sender) A:

The issue is identified. The email no-reply@<my-company-name>.com had failed its domains authentication requirements. It was being spoofed by Gmail and inappropriately forwarded (into spam) by proton mail.

There can be a documentation specific post on Stack Overflow (which can start hosting documentation centric posts in the future, just an idea I had) and so if anyone knows the details of what "authentication requirements" actually mean, this post will add even more value. As for me, I have found a hint big enough for me to know what direction to take from here. I am grateful to you all. Thanks!

Q: PyTorch training issue with EfficientNetB3 | Validation Accuracy plateu A:

There is an article that classifies japanese kanji characters (Using fastai to classify Japanese kanji characters | Towards Data Science) which may be worth a look.

Assuming there is proper class balance.

There could still be a couple problems with your approach

Try using “1Cycle Learning Rate Policy” which ramps up the learning rate then down which is could help break through validation plateaus.

Next, EfficientNet is pretrained on RGB images. Using it with single-channel input requires either duplicating the channel or adjusting the first conv layer which affects transfer learning quality.

unfreezing at epoch 3 is very early. Also, when the backbone unfreezes the optimizer and scheduler arent updated to give the newly unfrozen parameters good learning rates. This might cause issues as well with plateaus.

The number of classes is a lot thus you could try arc face loss (https://yiwenlai.medium.com/how-to-train-with-arcface-loss-to-improve-model-classification-accuracy-d4035195aeb9)

LR of 0.001 is aggressive for fine tuning a pretrained efficent net on a new domain (grayscale Kanji). A lower LR with differential learning rates

  • Lower LR for backbone
  • Higher LR for the head

Also keep use higher resolutions [max (300 x 300)] and try to visualize as much you can to see patterns and to check your models work (inferenced images, images per class, etc) that will help in the long term and to improve your models! Good luck!

Q: `perl -0pe` wants `.\n^`, not `.$\n^` A:

Add -w to see a warning message:

cat test.txt | perl -w -0pe 's/.$\n^text/hellohello/smg'
Possible unintended interpolation of $\ in regex at -e line 1.
Use of uninitialized value $\ in regexp compilation at -e line 1, <> chunk 1.
this

-w has the same effect as the use warnings pragma.

$\ is a special variable: OUTPUT_RECORD_SEPARATOR

Q: Tkinter button does not display text after being pressed A:

I think you need to convert the monthly_payment value to a string in order for it to show in the window. Something like:

monthly_payment_label = tk.Label(window, text=F'{monthly_payment}') # format to string

Q: vba date filter criteria derived from a cell reference A:

Hi after run this macro > for sheet2;

Make sure the cell you are referencing in Sheet2 (e.g., A1) contains an actual underlying Excel date. For example, if you want October 2013, you can type 10/1/2013 (or whatever your local format is) into A1, and you can use Excel's standard cell formatting to make it display as 10-2013. The VBA will read the underlying date perfectly.A dapt the cells and sheet names if necessary.

Sub FilterByDateFromCell()
    Dim wsData As Worksheet
    Dim wsCriteria As Worksheet
    Dim filterDate As Date
    Dim dateString As String
    
    ' Define your worksheets
    Set wsData = ThisWorkbook.Sheets("Sheet1")
    Set wsCriteria = ThisWorkbook.Sheets("Sheet2")
    
    ' 1. Get the date from Sheet2 (Change "A1" to wherever your date actually is)
    ' Ensure the cell in Sheet2 contains a real Excel date, even if formatted as MM-YYYY
    If Not IsDate(wsCriteria.Range("A1").Value) Then
        MsgBox "The criteria cell does not contain a valid date.", vbExclamation
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    filterDate = wsCriteria.Range("A1").Value
    
    ' 2. Format the date for the AutoFilter Array
    ' The array expects the 1st day of the month formatted strictly as US "m/d/yyyy"
    ' We use DateSerial to guarantee it's the 1st of the month
    dateString = Format(DateSerial(Year(filterDate), Month(filterDate), 1), "m/d/yyyy")
    
    ' 3. Apply the filters
    With wsData.Range("$A$2:$P$2173")
        ' Clear any existing filters first (optional but recommended)
        If wsData.AutoFilterMode Then wsData.AutoFilterMode = False
        
        ' Filter Field 13: Blanks OR the specified month
        ' The '1' in Criteria2:=Array(1, dateString) tells Excel to filter by the MONTH level
        .AutoFilter Field:=13, Criteria1:=Array("="), Operator:=xlFilterValues, Criteria2:=Array(1, dateString)
        
        ' Filter Fields 12 and 3 for non-blanks
        .AutoFilter Field:=12, Criteria1:="<>"
        .AutoFilter Field:=3, Criteria1:="<>"
    End With
    
End Sub
